title: Efficient GNN Training on Giant Graphs with Collective Batching and Scheduling
note: MorphGL adaptively splits mini-batch preparation between CPU and GPU on a single CPU GPU machine; explicitly a one-node system that adapts to the host CPU GPU balance

title: NEXT: A New Secondary Index Framework for LSM-based Data Storage
note: Secondary index framework for LSM-based key-value stores

title: A Unified and Efficient Coordinating Framework for Autonomous DBMS Tuning
note: Coordinating framework for multiple ML-based DBMS tuning agents (knobs, index, view) - ML-based tuning. Concern: no artifact link found in the arXiv preprint (2303.05710) or via search

title: BOSS - An Architecture for Database Kernel Composition
note: composable DBMS kernel architecture gluing Arrow, Velox and ArrayFire; builds in user space, one GPU

title: NEO: Saving GPU Memory Crisis with CPU Offloading for Online LLM Inference
note: CPU-offloaded attention and KV cache for online LLM inference - explicitly designed for one GPU plus host CPU, evaluated on T4/A10G which are weaker than the A5000, and the 16-core/125 GB host is exactly the regime it targets

title: MesaFS: An I/O-Efficient Metadata Service for Distributed File Systems
note: Metadata store that removes extra SSD writes from divided updates and layout ordering - the storage engine itself is single-node and user space. Concerns: framed as a distributed file system service and no code was found

title: Hawkeye: Reproducing GPU-Level Non-Determinism
note: Bit-exact CPU replay of NVIDIA Tensor Core matmuls; the paper explicitly tests Ampere along with Hopper and Lovelace, so the target GPU is a validated platform. Pure user-space tooling with no privileged access required - an unusually clean fit

title: Parrot: Efficient Serving of LLM-based Applications with Semantic Variable
note: Semantic Variable abstraction and DAG-aware scheduling for LLM applications - user-space Python serving layer. Concern - published numbers use multi-GPU deployments so experiments need to be scaled to one A5000 with smaller models

title: SEMA: A High-performance System for LLM-based Semantic Query Processing
note: Semantic query engine built on DuckDB with adaptive execution operator fusion and prompt handling for LLM operators. Concern: end-to-end numbers depend on LLM API latency and cost

title: When will my ML Job finish? Toward providing Completion Time Estimates through Predictability-Centric Scheduling
note: GPU-cluster scheduling for predictable completion times - main evaluation is a trace-driven simulator with only a small optional GPU testbed which is exactly the kind of scheduling study this machine supports. Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/TuftsNATLab/PCS/tree/osdi24-artifact .

title: How Good are Learned Cost Models, Really? Insights from Query Optimization Tasks
note: Systematic evaluation of learned cost models in query optimization; reproduction-friendly, single node

title: Extending Applications Safely and Efficiently
note: bpftime runs eBPF-style extensions entirely in *user space* via dynamic binary rewriting - that is the whole point of the paper, so unprivileged_bpf_disabled=2 does not block it; mature repo, Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concerns: the isolation story uses Intel MPK/PKU, which must be verified on this Zen3 Threadripper; and the kernel-eBPF comparison baselines in the paper need root, so those numbers cannot be re-measured.

title: cuMatch: A GPU-based Memory-Efficient Worst-case Optimal Join Processing Method for Subgraph Queries with Complex Patterns
note: GPU worst-case-optimal join with explicit GPU memory efficiency goals; single GPU

title: NDD: A Decision Diagram for Network Verification
note: Self-contained user-space decision-diagram library (BDD/BCDD/ZDD backends) benchmarked against CUDD/BuDDy/JDD; CPU+RAM only, no root, no network hardware. Claimed 100x memory and 100x time reduction is a clear, measurable improvement axis. Concern: none for the machine; the improvement would be data-structure/algorithm engineering rather than a distributed-systems build.

title: VectorCDC: Accelerating Data Deduplication with Vector Instructions
note: Content-defined chunking accelerated with SSE/AVX - pure user-space C++ benchmark tool (DedupBench), no root, no special hardware, builds with plain gcc. Concerns - Zen 3 Threadripper has SSE-128 and AVX-256 but no AVX-512, so the AVX-512 numbers cannot be reproduced; only hashless CDC variants (AE, MAXP, RAM) are vectorized, and the DEB dataset lives on Kaggle (download size to check).

title: Flame: Simplifying Topology Extension in Federated Learning
note: Topology abstraction (TAG) for composing FL architectures; the Python SDK data plane runs standalone and the docs state the control plane is optional for running SDK examples, so multi-topology FL can be emulated with local processes on one host. Concern: the full system ("flame-in-a-box") expects minikube/Docker and Go tooling - Docker is unavailable, so only the SDK-level path is usable, and Go must be installed via conda.

title: SeqCDC: Hashless Content-Defined Chunking for Data Deduplication
note: Best machine fit in the venue: pure user-space single-threaded CPU chunking measured as MB/s on local files. The official DedupBench tool from the authors' lab lists SeqCDC and cites this exact paper, and the evaluation dataset is published on Kaggle. Concern: only ~257 GB free on /home, so the larger corpora must be subsetted.

title: Load and MLP-Aware Thread Orchestration for Recommendation Systems Inference on CPUs
note: Thread orchestration for recommendation-model inference on CPUs - pure user-space on a 16-core machine; concerns: scheduling decisions may need hardware counters and no official repo was found

title: Practical Parameterized Query Optimization via Efficient Plan Reuse and List-wise Ranking
note: learned parameterized query optimizer with plan reuse and list-wise ranking - learned system component - concern: no repo located

title: CAVE: Concurrency-Aware Graph Processing on SSDs
note: Out-of-core graph processing that tunes concurrent I/O to a single SSD; user space, no root, NVMe present

title: Solid State Drive Targeted Memory-Efficient Indexing for Universal I/O Patterns and Fragmentation Degrees
note: Memory-efficient approximate SSD index combining approximate indices with an LSM-tree - an algorithmic, trace-driven storage contribution. AE Available plus Functional. Concern - FTL work of this kind is usually evaluated on FEMU which needs KVM, so the repo must be confirmed to have a pure user-space simulator or trace-replay path

title: AlignedServe: Orchestrating Prefix-aware Batching to Build a High-throughput and Computing-efficient LLM Serving System
note: prefix-aware batching and batch-level scheduling for LLM serving - a request-scheduling mechanism - arXiv preprint 2605.23389 exists - concern: the GPU-prefetch-for-GPU path assumes two GPUs - no repo located

title: To Adapt or Not to Adapt, That is the Ski Question
note: online ski-rental strategy deciding when an adaptive filter should pay the I/O to adapt - storage filter artifact with released code

title: RALF: Accuracy-Aware Scheduling for Feature Store Maintenance
note: accuracy-aware scheduling policy for feature-store maintenance. Concern: paper runs on 800 cores, so the policy must be re-evaluated at reduced scale or on traces

title: TranSQL + : Serving Large Language Models with SQL on Low-Resource Hardware
note: serves LLM inference by compiling the computation graph into SQL for CPU-only, low-memory hardware - exactly a single-node inference system - concern: no repo located

title: STAlloc: Enhancing Memory Efficiency in Large-Scale Model Training with Spatio-Temporal Planning
note: GPU memory allocator that replaces the PyTorch caching allocator using spatio-temporal tensor lifetime planning - the allocator itself can be studied with small models on one GPU. Concern: paper targets large-scale training

title: Efficient Cooperation-Aware Key and Value Management for LLM Inference
note: Cooperation-aware head-level KV cache budget allocation; pure inference-time memory management that runs on one GPU

title: On-device Semantic Selection Made Low Latency and Memory Efficient with Monolithic Forwarding
note: Training-free early-exit ranking system for cross-encoder top-K selection - the inference technique runs fine on one GPU or CPU, artifact on Zenodo. Concern: paper targets edge hardware

title: Taming Latency-Memory Trade-Off in MoE-Based LLM Serving via Fine-Grained Expert Offloading
note: Fine-grained MoE expert offloading between GPU and CPU memory - exactly the single-GPU plus host-DRAM regime of this machine. 24 GB plus 125 GB RAM fits small MoE models

title: Approximation-First Timeseries Query At Scale
note: PromSketch is a sketch-based approximate cache layer for Prometheus and VictoriaMetrics rule queries; standalone user-space module

title: From Tokens to Layers: Redefining Stall-Free Scheduling for MoE Serving with Layered Prefill
note: Layer-group scheduling that removes chunked-prefill expert reloads in MoE serving; a pure scheduler change with released code. Concern: only small MoEs (a few B active, ~15B total or quantized) fit in 24 GB, so the memory-traffic claim must be re-validated at that scale

title: FIFO queues are all you need for cache eviction (S3-FIFO)
note: Pure trace-driven cache-eviction study plus a C implementation in libCacheSim; CPU only, no root, no GPU. Ideal fit for the machine and for an improvement-style hypothesis on eviction policy. Concerns - the 6594-trace corpus across 14 datasets is far larger than 257 GB free so a documented trace subset must be chosen; the throughput/scalability claims were made at 16 threads which the 16-core Threadripper matches well

title: NNSmith: Generating Diverse and Valid Test Cases for Deep Learning Compilers
note: DL-compiler fuzzing - pure user-space Python runs against TVM/ONNXRuntime on one machine  widely used open source

title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for On-Device LLM Compression and Acceleration
note: Weight-only 4-bit quantization plus the TinyChat W4A16 inference engine - a user-space, single-GPU artifact. Concern - the 70B-on-mobile headline is out of reach; scale-down to 7B/13B on the A5000 is the realistic target. Widely used code, low build risk.

title: FedCaSe: Enhancing Federated Learning with Heterogeneity-aware Caching and Scheduling
note: The contribution is an importance-aware on-device cache admission/eviction policy plus a client scheduler - a cache-policy paper wearing an FL hat. FL client populations are emulated on a single host (FedScale-style), so it fits the machine. Concern - the paper's scale (thousands of simulated clients) needs the storage/RAM budget checked; GPU use is light.

title: GIO: Generating Efficient Matrix and Frame Readers for Custom Data Formats by Example
note: Generates efficient matrix/frame readers for custom data formats - an ML data-loading/ingestion contribution in Apache SystemDS. Concern: code embedded in the SystemDS tree

title: CarbonScaler: Leveraging Cloud Workload Elasticity for Optimizing Carbon-Efficiency
note: Elastic resource-allocation policy for batch jobs driven by carbon intensity, with a greedy marginal-allocation scheduler, released code, carbon traces and job scaling profiles; the analytic/trace-driven half is fully reproducible on one machine, and ML-training and MPI scaling profiles can be re-measured locally on 16 cores plus one GPU. Concern: the reference prototype is a Kubernetes autoscaler evaluated on a commercial cloud, and this machine has no root, no Docker and no second node, so the k8s prototype path is closed and the project would have to live in the simulator or in a local process-level re-implementation.

title: MIDAS: Minimizing Write Amplification in Log-Structured Systems through Adaptive Group Number and Size Configuration
note: Analytical (UID + Markov-chain) model that adapts group count and size to minimize GC write amplification in log-structured systems. Main results come from a user-space simulator, separately released at https://github.com/sungkyun123/MiDAS-Simulation and archived at Zenodo 10409599 - that part runs anywhere. Concern: the hardware prototype needs a Xilinx VCU108 FPGA with custom NAND modules that the authors state are not publicly available, so only the simulation-based claims are reproducible here. That is still a complete improvement target (the WAF/throughput comparisons against state-of-the-art GC are simulator results).

title: X-RLFLOW: GRAPH REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FOR NEURAL NETWORK SUBGRAPHS TRANSFORMATION
note: Reinforcement-learning agent replacing greedy search in tensor-graph superoptimization on top of TASO - runs on one GPU with small models - concern - depends on building TASO which is an older CUDA or cuDNN codebase

title: Cooperative Concurrency Control for Write-Intensive Key-Value Workloads
note: In-memory key-value store concurrency control on multicore CPUs - pure user space  fits 16-core host  AE artifact released on Zenodo

title: Flashlight: PyTorch Compiler Extensions to Accelerate Attention Variants
note: PyTorch compiler extension that auto-generates fused FlashAttention-style kernels for arbitrary attention variants, compared against FlexAttention. Single GPU; FlashAttention-2 style kernels are supported on Ampere

title: Removing Obstacles before Breaking Through the Memory Wall: A Close Look at HBM Errors in the Field
note: The artifact ships both the released HBM error dataset and the hierarchical failure-prediction pipeline, so it is a fully trace-driven learned-prediction study that runs on CPU here. Concern: it is a field study, so an improvement has to come from better prediction models or features rather than from a system change

title: LDB: An Efficient Latency Profiling Tool for Multithreaded Applications
note: Software-only latency profiler using LLVM instrumentation plus a busy-polling stack-scanning thread; explicitly designed to avoid hardware performance counters and kernel support, which matches a machine with perf_event_paranoid=3 and eBPF disabled. Concerns: requires building a custom LLVM 14 in user space (long build); dedicates one core to the scanner (fine on 32 threads); some applications evaluated in the paper are kernel-bypass runtimes that cannot run here, so plain Linux workloads must be substituted.

title: TAO: Tolerance-Aware Optimistic Verification for Floating-Point Neural Networks
note: Tolerance-aware optimistic verification of floating-point neural network execution - user-space verification running against a local GPU. No code found yet

title: CEMU: Enabling Full-System Emulation of Computational Storage beyond Hardware Limits
note: Emulator for computational-storage devices, a user-space storage research vehicle. Concern: QEMU-based full-system emulation without /dev/kvm falls back to TCG and will be slow

title: Improving LZ4 for Effective Compression and Efficient Query
note: improved LZ4 variant supporting direct query over compressed data, implemented in Apache TsFile - compression plus storage engine work - concern: no repo located

title: SAVE: Software-Implemented Fault Tolerance for Model Inference against GPU Memory Bit Flips
note: Software fault tolerance that splits model inference state across reliable and unreliable GPU memory; single-GPU, user-space bit-flip injection, and it was already evaluated on consumer-class GPUs including a 4090. Concern: the reliable-memory abstraction assumes accelerator features that may need emulation on the A5000

title: GenJoin: Conditional Generative Plan-to-Plan Query Optimizer that Learns from Subplan Hints
note: learned query optimizer that generates plan hints for PostgreSQL - learned component inside a system - CPU-only training is feasible

title: Rethinking Learned Index and LSM-tree Integration
note: Wild Turkey integrates learned indexes into LSM-trees with an RL controller for SSTable sizing and error bounds; RocksDB-based single-node artifact

title: Adaptive Quotient Filters
note: Filter/auxiliary-structure design for KV stores; pure user-space C/C++ data structure, trivially fits one machine

title: Hybrid Learning and Optimization-Based Dynamic Scheduling for DL Workloads on Heterogeneous GPU Clusters
note: RLTune combines an RL prioritizer with MILP job-to-node mapping and is trained and evaluated entirely on public traces (Microsoft Philly, Helios, Alibaba) - a trace-driven simulation that needs no GPU cluster. Repo URL is cited in the paper itself. Concern - repo quality and MILP solver licensing were not verified beyond a desk check.

title: Navigating Labels and Vectors: A Unified Approach to Filtered Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: Graph index for filtered ANN search; single-machine in-memory

title: Focus! Fast On-disk Concurrency-control Using Sketches
note: approximate timestamp store making timestamp-based concurrency control practical for disk-based KV stores - evaluated on SplinterDB - user-space storage systems work - concern: no repo located

title: Can Large Language Models Predict Data Correlations from Column Names?
note: A learned component for database tuning - predicting column correlations from schema text to prioritize data profiling and correct cardinality estimates, benchmarked against classical correlation-detection algorithms. Artifact plus benchmark are released. Machine fit is easy: the paper fine-tunes DistilBERT/ALBERT/RoBERTa on a single V100 (p3.2xlarge), all of which fit in 24 GB, and a modern 7-8B instruct model in FP16 also fits on the A5000 for an "improvement" angle. Concerns: this is a study rather than a system, so the improvement must be framed as a better predictor plus a demonstrated downstream benefit (e.g. feeding an optimizer), otherwise it degenerates into a pure reproduction - acceptable as the fallback track but worth flagging. [PVLDB 16(13), added from the vldbgap-2024 shard]

title: Paella - Low-latency Model Serving with Software-defined GPU Scheduling
note: User-space GPU kernel-granularity scheduler for DNN inference serving; README states it was tested on NVIDIA driver 535.54 and CUDA 12.2 which matches our driver 535.216 exactly, and CUDA arch is a build flag so sm_86 works. Single GPU by design. Concerns - needs LLVM/Clang 14, Boost, spdlog and a custom TVM fork all built from source into $HOME; the custom TVM build is long; MPS-style kernel interception should work unprivileged but is untested here

title: A Compilation-Based Under-Constrained Execution Engine
note: Compiles individual kernel components into native user-space harnesses and fuzzes them (AFL++) - the *analysis* runs in user space even though the target is kernel code, so no kernel build/boot is needed. Concern: LLVM toolchain must be built per-user; large compile times

title: SPFresh - Incremental In-Place Update for Billion-Scale Vector Search
note: On-disk vector index with an in-place rebalancing protocol (LIRE); an SSD-aware user-space storage engine on a single node, and the machine has two NVMe drives. Concerns - the default storage layer is SPDK, and the README explicitly requires secure boot off and kernel lockdown disabled for user-space PCI/NVMe access, which we cannot do without root; a modified-RocksDB backend is offered as an alternative and would have to be used; billion-scale datasets exceed 257 GB so 10M-100M subsets are needed; build uses gcc-9 and several apt-only libs that must be sourced through conda

title: MaxEmbed: Maximizing SSD bandwidth utilization for huge embedding models serving
note: Maximizes NVMe bandwidth for SSD-resident embedding tables in recommendation serving; the machine has two PM9A3 NVMe drives. Concern - if the artifact needs SPDK-style raw device binding that requires root, an io_uring path would have to be used instead.

title: Exploiting Structure in Regular Expression Queries
note: BLARE: multi-armed-bandit runtime strategy layered on existing regex libraries (RE2, PCRE2, Boost, ICU) - a user-space runtime/adaptive-execution artifact that builds and runs without root

title: Turbo - Effective Caching in Differentially-Private Databases
note: A caching/admission mechanism (PMW-Bypass) for DP query answering; Python core driven by Ray, CPU only, single machine, no root. Clean target for a policy-improvement hypothesis. Concerns - the artifact packages itself with Docker images which are not installable here, so deps must be replicated by hand with conda/pip; Covid and Citibike datasets must be regenerated by the provided scripts

title: TLP: A Deep Learning-Based Cost Model for Tensor Program Tuning
note: Learned cost model for tensor-program tuning - trains and runs on one GPU  open source  a natural target for better models or cheaper search

title: ZipLLM: Efficient LLM Storage via Model-Aware Synergistic Data Deduplication and Compression
note: Model-aware delta compression (BitX) plus tensor-level deduplication for LLM model-hub storage - CPU and disk only, no GPU needed, and Hugging Face model families are freely downloadable. Excellent fit for the 16-core/125 GiB/257 GB machine. Concern - the full Hugging Face characterization is petabyte scale so the study must be scoped to a few model families.

title: GMLake: Efficient and Transparent GPU Memory Defragmentation for Large-scale DNN Training with Virtual Memory Stitching
note: GPU virtual-memory stitching allocator inside the PyTorch caching allocator. Concern - paper uses A100 80 GB; on a 24 GB A5000 the study must use smaller models or LoRA/recompute settings, but the fragmentation mechanism is unchanged.

title: SHADE: Enable Fundamental Cacheability for Distributed Deep Learning Training
note: Importance-sampling-aware caching layer for the deep-learning training data pipeline, implemented in user space on top of PyTorch's DataLoader plus a key-value cache. Concern: the paper evaluates distributed DLT across multiple nodes and GPUs; here it would have to be scaled down to one node with one RTX A5000, which is a meaningful scale-down but changes the I/O-vs-compute balance the paper leans on. Also assumes a remote/slow backing store - that would have to be emulated locally (e.g. FUSE or cgroup I/O limits), which is doable without root.

title: Tally: Non-Intrusive Performance Isolation for Concurrent Deep Learning Workloads
note: Thread-block-level GPU kernel scheduling for concurrent DL workloads, implemented by intercepting CUDA in user space on a single GPU - excellent fit

title: OneAdapt: Fast Adaptation for Deep Learning Applications via Backpropagation
note: Configuration adaptation for DNN inference on streaming video using gradients through the codec; single-GPU inference pipeline, user space. Code URL is cited in the paper itself (reference [8]). Concern: repo has no README and many SLURM-oriented batch scripts, so setup effort is real; video datasets must be downloaded.

title: Diagnosing Performance Issues in Application-Defined Resources
note: User-space profiler (gigiprofiler) combining LLM semantic inference with static analysis, evaluated on MariaDB/Redis-class applications on one host. Concern: it "integrates with perf to sample hardware counters" - perf_event_paranoid=3 blocks that path, so only the instrumentation/LLM part is reproducible

title: MPK: A Compiler and Runtime for Mega-Kernelizing Tensor Programs
note: Mature open compiler/runtime (Mirage Persistent Kernel) that fuses an entire model into one persistent CUDA kernel; single-GPU megakernels are the base case and the AE branch tgx-osdi26-ae plus Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20563064 are pinned. Concerns: the multi-GPU communication-overlap contribution is unreachable; SM-level scheduling was tuned on newer architectures, so Ampere (cc 8.6, no TMA/FP8) may need retuning

title: GL-Cache: Group-level learning for efficient and high-performance caching
note: Excellent fit. A learned cache-eviction policy (group-level learning with XGBoost-style utility models) built on Segcache, evaluated by trace-driven simulation over 118 public block-I/O and CDN traces. Entirely user space, CPU only, no root. Traces (CloudPhysics, Twitter, Wiki/CDN) are public downloads; main cost is disk space for traces, which fits in the ~257 GB free. Strong improvement targets: group formation heuristics, feature set, learning cadence.

title: DynaFlow: Transparent and Flexible Intra-Device Parallelism via Programmable Operator Scheduling
note: Intra-device parallelism via programmable operator scheduling - by construction a single-GPU contribution, integrated into six ML systems with released code, and compatible with CUDA Graphs and TorchInductor. Very strong fit

title: Cabin: A Compressed Adaptive Binned Scan Index
note: Compressed scan index for main-memory analytics; CPU/SIMD only

title: Training with Confidence: Catching Silent Errors in Deep Learning Training with Automated Proactive Checks
note: TrainCheck is a Python instrumentation/invariant-inference layer over PyTorch; Available + Functional + Reproduced. Concern: a subset of the 20 reproduced silent-error cases involve DeepSpeed/multi-GPU configurations that cannot be recreated on one 24 GB GPU - the single-GPU subset is still substantial.

title: LiBox: A Learned Index as an Array to Minimize Last-Mile Search
note: Learned index that reduces last-mile search to a single SIMD step. Concern: the key mechanism uses an AVX-512 instruction and this Zen 3 Threadripper has no AVX-512 so the headline result cannot be reproduced without an AVX2 fallback

title: REmatch: a novel regex engine for finding all matches
note: User-space regular-expression engine enumerating all matches with output-linear delay; C++ library, CPU-only

title: SwiftFL: Enabling Speculative Training for On-Device Federated Deep Learning
note: Speculative training with gradient prediction for federated learning - the artifact is built on FederatedScope and installs through conda, so clients can be simulated on one host. Concern: paper frames it as on-device FL

title: PlanB: Efficient Software IPv6 Lookup with Linearized B+-Tree
note: Linearized B+-tree for IPv6 longest-prefix match - a pure user-space data-structure and memory-layout contribution benchmarked with real BGP FIB dumps; ideal single-machine CPU study. Concern - the paper reports cache-level analysis that we cannot reproduce without hardware perf counters.

title: VBASE: Unifying Online Vector Similarity Search and Relational Queries via Relaxed Monotonicity
note: Single-node query engine embedding vector indices into PostgreSQL; entirely user-space, CPU-bound, datasets fit the 257 GB of free disk. Concern: the released build is normally driven through containers, so the Dockerfile would have to be ported to a conda/source build. AE artifact mirror is https://github.com/Catoverflow/VBASE-artifacts .

title: Rethinking Learned Cost Models: Why Start from Scratch?
note: Learned cost models for query optimization, transferability across databases. Concern: no artifact found in GitHub search, repo unknown

title: Model Selection for Latency-Critical Inference Serving
note: RAMSIS generates model-selection/scheduling policies from a statistical model of query arrivals; policy generation is pure CPU work and serving uses a small ImageNet model zoo that fits 24 GB. Concern - the paper's worker pool is emulated across several GPUs; a single-GPU or simulated-worker scale-down is needed

title: The Case For Language Model Approximated LIKE Predicate
note: small language model that decodes LIKE patterns into candidate sets inside the database - learned component replacing an index path - small model fits easily - concern: no repo located
